events.extended_summary: On November 11 at about 9 p.m., two men believed to be British tourists stole a golden sculpture of Jesus Christ from the inner courtyard of the Shrine of Divine Mercy church on Dominikonų Street in Vilnius. CCTV footage shows one man, wearing a long grey coat and stripy scarf and speaking with an English accent, laughing as he holds the statue before another man in a turquoise hat. As he hoists the statue aloft, its arms break off, causing the golden figure to fall onto the cobblestones and shatter into pieces. The men flee the scene, and a passing car crushes some remains. The church's priest, Fr. Elijas Anatolijus Markauskas, shared the footage and appealed for information. Vilnius Police are investigating and initiated a pre-trial investigation under Article 284 of the Criminal Code while assessing the damage.
events.micro_summary: Two men believed to be British tourists shattered a golden Jesus statue stolen from a Vilnius church on November 11.
events.summary: CCTV shows two men, believed to be drunk British tourists, dropping and shattering a golden Jesus statue stolen from the Shrine of Divine Mercy church in Vilnius on November 11 before fleeing; police are investigating.

events.extended_summary: An EU ban on Russian liquefied natural gas imports starting January 1, 2027 will force Moscow to find new buyers for exports from Yamal, its flagship Arctic project, and reorganize shipping networks. Between January and October 2026, 81% of Yamal's recorded deliveries were destined for Europe, costing €8.7 billion. The ban ends long-term contracts tying Yamal to Europe, requiring redirection of gas most likely to Asian buyers. Longer voyages to Asia mean higher costs and fewer trips per tanker annually. Possible workarounds include virtual swaps where Russia sells gas to countries like Turkey or China, which then sell other gas to Europe, or increased black market trade, though LNG carriers are fewer and easier to track than oil tankers.
events.micro_summary: Starting 2027, Europe will stop buying Russian LNG from Yamal, forcing Moscow to redirect exports to Asia.
events.summary: An EU ban on Russian liquefied natural gas imports starting January 1, 2027 will force Moscow to redirect Yamal LNG exports to Asia, requiring longer voyages, costlier ships, and new logistics chains as 81% of recent deliveries went to Europe.

events.extended_summary: Molly Callahan, a 30-year-old gynecological teaching assistant, undergoes up to 16 speculum examinations on her busiest days to help medical students practice pap smears and breast exams before working with actual patients. Working across 30 universities and hospitals in the New York tri-state area, Callahan also serves as president of an international association for gynecological and male urogenital teaching associates. She states the procedure is not physically painful, telling those who view it as torture to "fire your gynecologist," though she notes the actual pap smear cell collection is abrasive and she could not perform 16 consecutively. Pap smears have reduced cervical cancer-related deaths by 86%, yet a study found 32% of women aged 21-29 and 15% of women aged 30-65 had never had one from 2005 to 2023. Teaching assistants became common in the 1970s after pelvic exams were historically performed on anesthetized patients.
events.micro_summary: Molly Callahan undergoes up to 16 speculum exams daily to train medical students in gynecological procedures.
events.summary: Gynecological teaching assistant Molly Callahan undergoes up to 16 speculum exams daily to train medical students in pap smears and breast exams, stating the procedure is not painful and urging patients to demand better care from gynecologists.

events.extended_summary: A four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop—the longest in 25 years—canceled more than 8,000 flights Friday after an aging air traffic control system became overloaded with data, causing inconsistencies in router information. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the system was shut down due to the data issues and warned that resuming normal operations would take time. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated there was no indication of a nefarious attack. By Saturday morning, more than 3,000 additional flights had been canceled as airlines scrambled to recover, leaving passengers stranded at airports including Boston, Washington DC, New York and Miami. The disruption affected sports teams, forcing the rescheduling of Mississippi's college football game against Oklahoma to Sunday and postponing a men's basketball game between UNC Greensboro and Cornell. While Duffy said operations were slowly returning to normal Saturday, delays and cancellations continued nationwide.
events.micro_summary: Over 8,000 flights were canceled Friday during the longest nationwide FAA ground stop in 25 years.
events.summary: A four-hour nationwide FAA ground stop—the longest in 25 years—canceled over 8,000 flights Friday after an aging air control system became overloaded with data, with thousands more canceled Saturday as operations slowly resumed.

events.extended_summary: US President Donald Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's President Vladimir Putin will hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, from November 18-19. The talks will focus on nuclear proliferation, including the lapsed New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty, as well as the ongoing war in Iran and Russia's war in Ukraine. The meeting comes amid global turbulence including the closure of the Strait of Hormuz for over 100 days and trade tensions between Washington and Beijing. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and others have expressed concern that the meeting could create a 'Yalta 2.0' moment where excluded nations face geopolitical trade-offs. Russia hopes to establish a new security framework in Europe, while China has shown reluctance to join nuclear agreements it did not help create.
events.micro_summary: Trump, Xi and Putin will hold their first trilateral meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19.
events.summary: US President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin will hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen from November 18-19 to discuss nuclear proliferation, the Iran war and Ukraine.

events.extended_summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused SpaceX of throttling the Starshield military satellite system across the entire frontline, imposing speed limits of 161km/h (100mph) on Ukrainian drones for five days. The restrictions prevented Ukrainian forces from intercepting incoming Russian jet-powered Shahed drones and conducting mid-range strikes against military targets in Russian-occupied territory. Zelenskyy characterized the decision as "political" rather than "technical," noting that SpaceX had told Kyiv there were "no restrictions." He said he had raised the issue with SpaceX, the Pentagon, and the US State Department, but received no clear explanation. Ukraine suspects the slowdown is a deliberate tactic to pressure Zelenskyy into making concessions to Russia, coinciding with US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi. This marks the second time in recent weeks that Starshield connectivity has been restricted over Russian-occupied territories. SpaceX denied the claims, stating the issue was technical.
events.micro_summary: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of throttling Starshield satellite system to 100mph across the frontline.
events.summary: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy accused SpaceX of imposing 100mph speed limits on the Starshield satellite system across the frontline for five days, disrupting drone interceptions and strikes, calling the move political rather than technical.

events.extended_summary: The first week of COP31 climate talks in Antalya concluded with leaders avoiding explicit mentions of fossil fuels despite mounting warnings that the world will overshoot the 1.5℃ threshold. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed leaders on 11 November, describing recent extreme weather as the "summer of truth" and stating the world is at a "global tipping point" on course to exceed the 1.5℃ target, yet her speech focused on electrification and partnerships without mentioning fossil fuels, which account for around 68 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions. Finland launched a domestic fossil fuel phaseout roadmap at the summit, joining France, Germany and the Netherlands, noting that over 96 per cent of its electricity already comes from non-fossil sources. Outgoing UN Secretary-General António Guterres delivered a farewell address declaring climate action central to the UN's work, warning "you cannot build peace on a burning planet," as leaders departed leaving negotiators to address electrification and just transition.
events.micro_summary: COP31 leaders avoid fossil fuel mentions as UN chief warns of 1.5℃ overshoot.
events.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, leaders wrapped the first week avoiding fossil fuel mentions despite warnings of overshooting 1.5℃, while Finland launched a phaseout roadmap and outgoing UN chief António Guterres urged climate action as central to global governance.

events.extended_summary: Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text in obsolete Gabelsberger shorthand within 16 notebooks from the early 1940s. Since 2017, Jan von Plato led a Helsinki University project to decipher the material, with progress averaging about a page per week until September, when the AI model Claude was enlisted. Within a couple of days, Claude provided a comprehensive digest revealing that Gödel had proved hundreds of theorems that no one knew about. The workbooks contain dozens of anticipations of results not known until the 70s and 80s, plus 14 themes in logic that have not been pursued. Gödel, whose 1931 incompleteness theorems transformed mathematics, fled Austria in 1940 and died in 1978.
events.micro_summary: AI decoded Kurt Gödel's 1,009 pages revealing hundreds of theorems no one knew about in his 1940s workbooks.
events.summary: AI model Claude decoded 1,009 pages of Kurt Gödel's 1940s workbooks in obsolete Gabelsberger shorthand, revealing hundreds of theorems no one knew about and 14 logic themes not pursued within days.

The Cop31 climate summit in Antalya is thought to be the largest ever in the three decades of the annual gatherings, with more than 92,000 delegates registered to attend talks aimed at shifting the world away from the fossil fuels that are dangerously overheating our planet. This swell of people includes numerous groups that support or are influenced by coal, oil and gas interests, the review has found. In total, 103 groups with a track record of obstructing climate action or furthering fossil fuel interests are at Cop31, according to the Kick Big Polluters Out coalition, which comprises about 450 environmental organisations. events.extended_summary: Microsoft fully restored its Outlook, Teams and Copilot services early Saturday morning after a worldwide outage that began Thursday around 1pm ET and lasted nearly 24 hours. The disruption, caused by a network capacity upgrade rather than a cyber-attack, affected more than 70 countries and over 430 million users worldwide. Institutions impacted included the Japanese government, the Philippines Supreme Court, the Australian spy agency, hospitals and courts across North America, the UK's NHS, Canadian rail networks, Singapore's government, and officials at Turkey's COP31 climate summit. In the US, the House of Representatives lost a day of legislative work, while local impacts ranged from Arapahoe County, Colorado, where a detention facility could not process online bond payments, to Los Angeles County's sheriff's department and emergency management services in Texas unable to receive emails. UK officials noted limited impact on critical services like 999 calls. Experts described the event as a stark reminder of global reliance on major technology providers.
events.micro_summary: Microsoft restored worldwide services after an outage affecting 430 million users across 70 countries.
events.summary: Microsoft restored Outlook, Teams and Copilot services early Saturday after a worldwide outage lasting nearly 24 hours disrupted operations in over 70 countries, affecting more than 430 million users and institutions including governments, hospitals and courts.

events.extended_summary: Colorado trailed by 13 late in the second quarter Friday against Houston. Then it scored the game’s next 28 points. That spurt helped Deion Sanders’ Buffaloes upset the No. 14 Cougars 42-32, shaking up the Big 12 title race and securing Colorado’s first win over an AP top-15 team since beating No. 3 Oklahoma on a last-second field goal on Sept. 29, 2007. Colorado was a 23-point underdog in that game and trailed 24-7 late in the third quarter before scoring the final 20 points. It had lost 35 games in a row against top-15 teams since then. Friday’s win sent fans spilling onto the field to celebrate at Folsom Field. “It was balance,” Sanders said. “We all caught the same bus. The offense showed up. The defense showed up. Special teams showed up. We all were here. Usually, somebody gets left. They get the wrong time on the itinerary.”
events.micro_summary: Colorado dashes Houston’s College Football Playoff hopes with first top-15 win since 2007.

events.extended_summary: Chelsea defeated defending champions Manchester City 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move to the top of the Women's Super League table. Sandy Baltimore scored the decisive goal with a fierce strike from inside the box on the stroke of half-time. City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita received a straight red card in the second half for a professional foul on Alyssa Thompson, reducing her side to ten players. The result leaves Chelsea one point ahead of City at the summit and ends Manchester City's unbeaten run this season, while Chelsea remain undefeated. City had several chances including a missed open goal by Lauren Hemp, but could not find an equalizer. Aggie Beever-Jones hit the post from a free-kick after Yamashita's dismissal.
events.micro_summary: Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 to leapfrog them at the top of the Women's Super League.
events.summary: Chelsea defeated Manchester City 1-0 at Stamford Bridge with Sandy Baltimore's first-half strike, moving one point clear at the top of the Women's Super League table and ending City's unbeaten season.

events.extended_summary: Carlton advanced to the AFLW preliminary finals after defeating Hawthorn 6.7 (43) to 6.2 (38) in a five-point semi final victory at Princes Park in front of 4,701 fans. Darcy Vescio kicked the match-winning goal in her 100th game, finishing with two goals as the Blues overcame a 19-point first-term deficit to claim the win. Hawthorn was without star midfielder Eliza West, who suffered a knee injury early in the final quarter after recording 31 disposals. Earlier, Sydney defeated Geelong by three points in the other semi final to progress to face North Melbourne. Carlton will now face Melbourne in the 2026 preliminary finals. Geelong's match was marred by a serious head injury to ruck Piper Dunlop.

events.extended_summary: US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The Ukrainian president's comments come after US President Donald Trump's envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable. Russia controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released
events.micro_summary: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says.

events.extended_summary: A tanker named Atlantic Asphalt collided with the American Heritage riverboat in the Port of New Orleans on Friday, causing the five-story cruise ship to topple over and sink in the Mississippi River. The vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines and built in 2015, was docked when struck while finishing an eight-day cruise. Nearly 200 people were on board; several plunged into the river and were rescued by first responders, tugboat operators, and police. Thirty-two people were transported to hospitals, though officials confirmed none had critical injuries. New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno stated that zero people were unaccounted for, calling it a miracle. The 520-foot-long vessel, sailing under a Marshall Islands flag, was struck as the tanker crossed under a nearby bridge. The cause remains under investigation, and a section of the river was closed to vessel traffic during the rescue operation.
events.micro_summary: A tanker collision sank a New Orleans riverboat Friday, hospitalizing 32 with no critical injuries.
events.summary: A tanker struck the American Heritage riverboat in New Orleans on Friday, causing it to topple and sink in the Mississippi River. Of nearly 200 aboard, 32 were hospitalized with no critical injuries, and all were accounted for.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian drones attacked an industrial zone in the southern Russian city of Volgograd, killing four people and injuring two. Falling debris caused localized fires at the Lukoil oil refinery, the largest in southern Russia, which processes around 14.8 million metric tons of crude oil annually. The facility had been attacked previously on October 2. Gasoline prices in Volgograd rose overnight by 50 kopeks per liter, prompting drivers to line up at stations. Russia’s Defense Ministry reported intercepting 1,198 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and annexed Crimea overnight. The strike was at least the eighth on a Russian oil refinery since October 30. The attack came a day after U.S. envoys met with Russian and Ukrainian leaders in Moscow and Dublin.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian drones killed four people in an attack on a Volgograd oil refinery.
events.summary: Ukrainian drones attacked a major Volgograd oil refinery, killing four people and injuring two, while Russia said it intercepted 1,198 drones overnight.

events.extended_summary: Baththa won the Best Feature Film award at the India Film Festival of Alberta (IFFA) 2026 and was included in the festival's Official Selection. Actor Sai Prithviraj received a Special Mention in the Best Actor category for his performance. Directed by Balaji Tharaneetharan and presented by Star Studio18 and Atlee, the film was released on October 1, 2026, and had a promising opening weekend with positive word of mouth. The film stars Vijay Sethupathi alongside Sai Prithviraj, Lijomol Jose, Ajay Ghosh and Arjun Chidambaram. The story revolves around an unlikely bond between a gangster and a young boy. Produced under Cine1 Studios and A For Apple Studios by Murad Khetani, Priya Atlee, Alok Jain and Ajit Andhare, with Ashwin Murugan as co-producer, the film has drawn appreciation for both Vijay Sethupathi's portrayal and Sai Prithviraj's natural expressions and emotionally engaging performance.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, collected Rs 47.85 crore net in India on its ninth day, bringing its domestic net total to Rs 612.45 crore. The film's worldwide gross has crossed Rs 1,110.70 crore, making it the 11th Indian film to surpass Rs 1,000 crore globally in just eight days. On Friday, November 13, the movie recorded 22,993 shows across India with an average collection of Rs 20,851 per show, though this represented a 10.6% decline from the previous day's Rs 53.50 crore. The Hindi version contributed Rs 36.25 crore from 18,377 shows, accounting for over 77% of domestic earnings, while Malayalam, Kannada, Tamil and Telugu added Rs 3.25 crore, Rs 3.00 crore, Rs 2.75 crore and Rs 2.60 crore respectively. The film's highest single-day collection remains Rs 107.50 crore recorded on Day 5.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend crosses Rs 1,110 crore worldwide gross in nine days.
events.summary: Ramayana: Rise of a Legend earned Rs 47.85 crore net in India on day nine, lifting domestic net to Rs 612.45 crore and worldwide gross beyond Rs 1,110 crore, the 11th Indian film to cross Rs 1,000 crore globally.

events.extended_summary: Pakistan has nominated Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik to represent the country at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilizational Dialogue in New Delhi from November 20 to 22, 2026. This marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in over three years, since Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari attended the SCO meeting in Goa in May 2023. India had invited Pakistan's Culture Minister Aurangzeb Khan Khichi, but Pakistan selected Malik instead. The forum, proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO summit in Tianjin, expects over 25 countries. Pakistan stated the government remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations within the SCO framework. The visit occurs amid strained relations following the April 2025 Pahalgam attack and India's Operation Sindoor. Pakistan assumed the SCO chairmanship for 2026-27 and will host the summit in Islamabad in August 2027.
events.micro_summary: Pakistan names Climate Minister Musadik Masood Malik for SCO dialogue in New Delhi November 20-22, first ministerial visit since 2023.
events.summary: Pakistan named Climate Minister Musadik Masood Malik for the SCO Civilizational Dialogue in New Delhi from November 20-22, marking the first Pakistani ministerial visit to India in over three years.

events.extended_summary: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal stated that India is on track to achieve its USD 1 trillion export target for the financial year ending March despite geopolitical disruptions. Speaking at the inauguration of the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on November 13, Goyal highlighted record October 2026 exports of nearly USD 90 billion, comprising USD 50 billion in merchandise and USD 40 billion in services. Cumulative exports for the first seven months reached USD 570 billion, while the first six months saw approximately USD 480 billion, or 48 percent of the annual target. Goyal projected trade expansion of 15 to 16 percent this year and noted engineering exports grew around 22 percent. He urged businesses to leverage Free Trade Agreements to help India become a developed nation by 2047.
events.micro_summary: India is on track to hit its USD 1 trillion export target this financial year, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said.
events.summary: India is on track to achieve its USD 1 trillion export target this financial year, Minister Piyush Goyal said, citing USD 570 billion in the first seven months and a record USD 90 billion in October.

events.extended_summary: India U19 defeated Pakistan U19 by one wicket in the Under-19 Asia Cup final at Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat, chasing down 338 to claim their 10th title. Pakistan posted 337/9 in 50 overs after Usman Khan scored 107 from 111 balls and Abdul Qadir smashed 80 from 54. India slumped to 252/8 before No. 10 Mohit Ulva produced an unbeaten 49 off 26 deliveries. With three runs needed off the final ball, Ulva charged down the track and hit Ahmed Hussain's delivery to the boundary at wide long-off, sealing victory. Captain Lakshya Raichandani contributed 80 and opener Aaryavir Sehwag made 58. Kavya Patel claimed 4/69 for India.
events.micro_summary: India U19 beat Pakistan U19 by one wicket chasing 338 in the Asia Cup final at Al Amerat.
events.summary: India U19 defeated Pakistan U19 by one wicket in the Asia Cup final at Al Amerat, chasing 338 after Mohit Ulva's unbeaten 49 sealed victory with a boundary off the final ball.

events.extended_summary: A speeding minibus collided head-on with a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam, killing 26 people and injuring 16 others, including around a dozen in critical condition. The accident occurred on NH-715 near Rangajan when the minibus, traveling from Golaghat to Nagaon, reportedly swerved across lanes at high speed and struck the truck heading toward Upper Assam. Dashcam footage showed the minibus approaching at high speed before jumping its lane. The vehicle had a history of traffic violations, including 12 challans and a fine for driving at 102 kmph. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma visited the site, suggested the driver may have suffered a stroke or was under the influence, and vowed to bring back strict traffic rules. He announced compensation for victims' families and ordered detailed post-mortem examinations. Speed restrictions of 20 kmph apply in animal corridors along the 60km stretch.
events.micro_summary: A minibus-truck collision near Kaziranga National Park killed 26 people and injured 16.
events.summary: A speeding minibus collided head-on with a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam, killing 26 people and injuring 16. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma visited the site and vowed to enforce strict traffic rules.

events.extended_summary: A significant fire broke out at an illegal textile waste warehouse near the Unn Patiya area and ANG Society on Kharwasa Canal Road in Surat district, Gujarat. The unauthorized facility covered approximately two bighas of land and stored fabric scraps without official permission. Nine fire tenders were deployed to the site to tackle the rapidly spreading blaze, which alarmed local residents in the nearby area. Firefighters attempted to douse the flames as tenders rushed to bring the fire under control. Concerns have been raised about how the unauthorized facility operated without detection by local authorities. Further details regarding the cause of the fire and the extent of the damage are awaited.
events.micro_summary: A fire broke out at an illegal textile waste warehouse in Surat, Gujarat, with nine fire tenders deployed.
events.summary: A fire erupted at an illegal textile waste warehouse near ANG Society in Surat, Gujarat. Nine fire tenders were deployed to tackle the blaze at the two-bigha facility storing fabric scraps without permission.

events.extended_summary: The death toll in a road accident near Kaziranga National Park in Assam's Golaghat district has risen to 26, with 24 victims identified and two still unidentified. The accident occurred on Friday when a passenger vehicle and a container truck collided head-on in the Rongajaan area. Nineteen injured people were initially sent to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital, where two later died. Among the deceased, nine were from Nagaon district, one from Karbi Anglong district, and one from Bihar, identified as 38-year-old Mohammad Rafiq Ali from Madhubani district. Three teams with 11 doctors from Guwahati Medical College and Jorhat Medical College are conducting post-mortems, with ambulances on standby. The district administration has arranged vehicles to transport bodies to hometowns and is assisting affected families. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma expressed deep grief over the loss.
events.micro_summary: Road accident near Kaziranga National Park kills 26, with 24 victims identified.
